persistence_checks: after a remote revoke or disable the Device B Room note set is unchanged
after a remote revoke or disable the Device B durable outbox is unchanged
LOCAL_ONLY notes remain local and account-scoped cached notes remain account-scoped and are never reassigned
an account in DELETION_PENDING leaves the Android local notes intact
a purge removes only the server account data and never touches Android local Room data
rotation_checks: a revoked refresh token never rotates into a new valid refresh chain
a retried rotation with the same refresh_request_id still recovers the same result
after in-grace cancellation the account is ACTIVE again and a fresh login or refresh succeeds
search_checks: exactly one session in the session list is flagged as the current installation
the two device instances hold distinct session ids and distinct installation identities on the same account
a concurrent write from the same base revision is answered with the authoritative 409 body and no silent overwrite
fixture_intent: Two independent Android device/app instances on ONE KeepLab account (two ADB-visible emulators, one physical device plus one emulator, or two physical devices), each with its own app process, local Room database, secure/session store, KeepLab-generated installation identity and authenticated session. The backend fixture is the existing development backend/test environment with two independent authenticated clients (distinct sessions and installation identities, same account); no cloud infrastructure is provisioned. The D-05 boundary fixture is an injected/fake server clock, never a 30-real-day wait.
oracle_intent: Deterministic only. Primary oracle: the deterministic backend tests, the deterministic two-client backend integration, the deterministic Android JVM tests, and explicit assertions on the two-device journey (persisted Room/outbox state, server-accepted revision, refused status codes, the fake-clock purge_after arithmetic, and the exact A8 gate values). Screenshots are never the primary oracle; on a device failure the evidence may include a screenshot plus the layout hierarchy, logcat and the failed assertion, read once. PUSH_PROVIDER = NONE and PUSH_REQUIRED_FOR_CORRECTNESS = NO are asserted, not assumed. The engine field records the stack's selector-driven device replay family; the real oracle is the deterministic assertions above. Verification runs once; PASS = STOP, and an unavailable real device pair yields A8_DEVICE_PAIR_UNAVAILABLE rather than a mock PASS.
